title: runtime-observation-enrichment-and-labeling-guidelines-2025
author: Elena Rodriguez
content:
Overview:
This document defines the canonical approach for enriching runtime telemetry (traces, kernel events, request metadata) with contextual labels and cost tags so downstream consumers (alerting, billing, profiler, experiments) can reliably join signals. The goal is consistent, low-cost enrichment that enables accurate SLO attribution, cost-per-inference accounting, and fidelity-aware debugging across hosted, dedicated and private deployments.

Why this matters:
- Inconsistent labels are the single largest source of signal fragmentation when debugging tail latency and kernel regressions.
- Cost and energy tags let product and finance teams reconcile per-route economics without pulling raw traces.
- Enriched, compact traces speed triage for oncall by surfacing the minimum causal set of attributes needed to reproduce or route incidents.

Principles:
1) Minimal, stable keyset: restrict primary labels to a small set that is unlikely to change (see Label Taxonomy).
2) Schema-first: all labels follow the canonical key names and types in this doc; any extension requires a review.
3) Cost-aware sampling: enrich higher-value requests at a higher sampling rate; inexpensive warmup traces sampled low.
4) Privacy & minimal PII: do not attach user PII or raw prompt text to traces. Use hashes or prompt-ids where needed.
5) Low-latency enrichment: enrichment must not add more than 1 ms on the request path in p95. Use asynchronous enrichers for non-blocking attributes.

Label taxonomy (canonical keys):
- request.id: stable UUID for the user request (string)
- route.name: product route or API path (string)
- model.variant: model name and variant (e.g., gptx-16q8) (string)
- kernel.path: kernel family / variant invoked (string)
- hw.pool: accelerator pool identifier (e.g., a100-pool-3) (string)
- cost.token_estimate: integer estimated token count (stringified integer)
- fidelity.flag: one of [full, approximate, degraded] (string)
- kvcache.hit_ratio: float (0.0-1.0) represented as string
- customer.tier: free | standard | enterprise (string)
- region: cloud region (string)
- trace.version: schema version (string)

Note: store numeric values as strings for telemetry pluggability and to avoid downstream parsing discrepancies.

Table: retention and storage hints (recommended):
- traces.enriched.retention: 30d (for fully enriched traces used in oncall workflows)
- traces.minimal.retention: 7d (for minimal traces used only for perf sampling)
- aggregated.metrics.retention: 365d
- cold-storage.export: weekly snapshots to S3 for compliance (retention 2y)

Sampling policy (high-level):
1) Baseline sampling: 0.5% of all requests capture minimal trace (spans + request.id + route.name).
2) Enriched sampling tiers:
   - High-value routes (customer.tier=enterprise or routes flagged by product): 20% enriched.
   - Potential-regressions: traffic flagged by the anomaly-detector (see procedure) gets 100% enrichment for 1h.
   - Manual oncall escalations: toggle enrich=true via /api/operator/enrich-toggle for the given route for immediate 15-minute capture.
3) Dynamic cost weighting: If cost.token_estimate > 10k, escalate enriched sampling by +5x for that request bucket.

Enrichment pipeline (component roles):
- Request Ingress (lightweight): attaches request.id, route.name, and region synchronously.
- Async Enricher (nonblocking): fetches model.variant, hw.pool membership, kvcache.hit_ratio from the runtime metadata service; annotates trace with these fields.
- Cost Estimator (streaming): estimates token count using header hints and concise tokenizer lookup; writes cost.token_estimate into trace.
- Privacy Redactor: replaces prompt text with prompt.id before long-term retention.

CLI examples:
- Toggle enrichment for route for 15m (operator):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" 
    https://internal-api.redwood.local/operator/enrich-toggle 
    -d '{"route":"/v1/chat/llm", "enrich": true, "duration_m":15}'

- Query enriched trace sample (example using internal tracer):
  rtr-cli get-trace --id 8a7f3c2b --compact=true

JSON example of a canonical enriched trace (compact):
{
  "trace.id": "8a7f3c2b-9c1d-4f8d-bf3a-abcdef012345",
  "route.name": "/v1/generate/completion",
  "model.variant": "redwood/longformer-32k-16q8",
  "kernel.path": "attention-sharded-v2",
  "hw.pool": "a100-pool-3",
  "cost.token_estimate": "1200",
  "fidelity.flag": "full",
  "kvcache.hit_ratio": "0.82",
  "customer.tier": "standard",
  "trace.version": "v1"
}

Enrichment performance budget:
- Synchronous enrichment: <1 ms p95
- Full async enrichment completion: <50 ms median, <200 ms p99
- Failure modes: if enricher times out, record enricher.timeout=true and proceed without fields to avoid on-path tail inflation.

Debugging and incident workflows (runbook excerpt):
1) If tail latency breach detected for route X:
   a) Check sampled enriched traces for route.name==X in the last 15m.
   b) Filter traces where fidelity.flag != full and compare kernel.path distributions.
   c) If kernel.path change or hw.pool migration is visible, escalate to runtime-kernel-oncall and attach 5 representative traces (use rtr-cli sample-attach).
2) If cost-per-inference anomalies observed:
   a) Aggregate cost.token_estimate by model.variant and route.name for the window.
   b) If sudden token estimate inflation, run tokenizer audit (tokenizer-audit --route X --window 1h).
   c) Notify SRE and product: add label incident.cost_inflation.

Extension and governance process:
- To add a new canonical label or change type, open an ADR and include: motivation, schema change, migration plan, and storage impact estimate.
- Small labels (non-critical) may be trialed as optional.enricher.* keys for 4 weeks before approval.

Table: enforcement thresholds and alerts:
- Missing trace.version on >1% enriched traces for 1h -> P2 alert to observability team.
- enricher.timeout > 0.5% of enriched traces in 5m -> P1 to runtime infra.
- prompt-id absent on any trace stored beyond 7d -> security incident, restrict retention immediately.

Operational rollout checklist (numbered):
1) Deploy async enricher v1 to canary fleet (10% traffic).
2) Run canary for 72h, monitor enricher.timeout and enrichment-completion latency.
3) Validate label presence against schema for 95% of enriched traces.
4) Run tokenizer-audit on canary traffic to confirm cost estimates alpha accuracy within 15%.
5) Gradual ramp to 100% canary-to-prod over 48h if all checks pass.

Appendix A — Example instrumenter snippet (Python):
# pseudo-code, meant for the runtime's tracer shim
from internal_tracer import start_span, annotate
span = start_span('request')
span.annotate('request.id', request_id)
span.annotate('route.name', route_name)
# schedule async enricher task
async_enricher.schedule(request_id, context_headers)

Appendix B — Migration notes for older schemas:
- Older traces used trace.schema v0 and stored model and kernel under model_info.*; ingestion pipeline must map model_info.name -> model.variant and kernel.variant -> kernel.path at read time. Backfill of trace.version=v1 is optional; if required, create a daily job to migrate high-value route traces first.
